status: complete; corrected deterministic causal integration released
title: J2 causal callback remediation and typed E1 schedule integration matrix
rigor_tier: deterministic correctness remediation and interface validation; no performance study

program_alignment.central_question: Can each schedule invoke the verified typed E1 D4 policy using only observations causally available at its decision time while all branches share one physical trace?
program_alignment.information_value: The matrix removes a demonstrated future-sensitive callback digest before connecting physical observations or producing downstream samples.

defect_and_knowledge_states.defect: Causal InnerDecoderRequest objects contain a digest of the complete visible history, including future rows, and their request/response digests depend on it.
defect_and_knowledge_states.minimal_counterfactual: Two histories identical through immediate invocation have identical prefix digests but different immediate request digests when only later rows change.
defect_and_knowledge_states.affected_prior_evidence: J2 causal request/response isolation is invalidated; no stochastic or performance data consumed it.
unaffected_prior_evidence: branch timing on the original fixture
defect_and_knowledge_states.smallest_supportable_claim: After remediation, causal callback outputs are invariant to every future-only record change, and verified typed E1 records can drive both public modes at each branch's invocation horizon.
competing_outcomes: Removing full-history identity from the callback restores causal invariance and integration passes.
Another request field or integration side channel remains future-sensitive and the causal branch stays invalid.
Causality is repaired but a round-local E1 record or D4 policy invariant fails, localizing integration rather than schedule timing.

model.shared_trace: one immutable SpacetimeRecord whose syndrome_readout and herald_readout arrays are the sole public source for both scheduling and round-local E1 reports
model.round_local_e1_record: at invocation round t, m_flux membership equals syndrome_readout[t] and e_charge membership equals herald_readout[t] at each D4 site
model.hidden_information: syndrome/herald truth decompositions, readout-fault masks, physical faults, future rows for causal branches, and logical outcomes
model.causal_callback: contains the causal prefix and prefix digest but no full-history digest; full-history identity remains outside the decoder callback in branch/run provenance
model.offline_callback: receives the final causal prefix and remains explicitly noncausal; a full-history digest is unnecessary because the final prefix digest already binds its visible record
model.policy_translation: typed_record_to_commit_request binds the callback prefix digest and round-local E1 report digest before invoking syndrome_only or heralded
model.resolution_limit: The study validates causal information flow and stage-1 policy invocation only, not post-action charge recovery, schedule advantage, or fault tolerance.

fork_classification.R1_callback_causality: prerequisite; run before all dependent integration cells
fork_classification.I2_mode_schedule_matrix: eight cheap reversible cells: two public modes by four schedule branches; run all
fork_classification.I3_negative_controls: future mutation, private-truth mutation, multi-label report, and explicit offline sensitivity; run all
fork_classification.performance_sampling: blocked until every registered cell passes

acceptance: full visible-history digest is absent from InnerDecoderRequest and request_digest
immediate output is invariant when only rounds after immediate invocation change
fixed-delay output is invariant when only rows after its invocation change
JIT output is invariant when only rows after its invocation change
offline remains explicitly noncausal and may change with final-history changes
branch/run provenance still binds all branches to one full visible-history digest outside the callback
the public E1 record is derived only from the last row of the supplied causal prefix
its round and trial identity match the invocation
flux and charge membership equal the public syndrome/herald bits site by site
changing private truth/fault decompositions without changing readouts leaves the record identical
future-only public changes leave every earlier causal E1 record identical
all cells invoke the actual public D4 stage-1 policy
both modes share the same trace, cluster timing, and scheduler configuration
each causal policy request binds only its invocation prefix and round-local E1 report
syndrome-only and heralded retain their verified information budgets
multi-label public rows execute in heralded mode without coercion
deterministic replay is bit identical
future-only mutations do not change earlier causal D4 requests or actions
private truth-only mutations do not change any public request or action
an odd reported flux syndrome fails closed at the existing policy invariant
offline outputs remain explicitly labeled noncausal

budget.compute: under five CPU minutes and 1 GiB

analysis_and_stop_rules.success: R1 passes before I1-I3, and all eight mode/schedule cells execute with causal invariance where declared.
analysis_and_stop_rules.localized_negative: Preserve unaffected branch timing and truth-exclusion evidence while marking any future-sensitive or policy-invalid cell unresolved.
analysis_and_stop_rules.stop: Do not weaken digest binding, hide a failed causal cell, add stochastic samples, or implement post-action recovery to compensate for a stage-1 failure.
analysis_and_stop_rules.escalation: Ask the researcher only if repairing causality requires changing the accepted information budget or abandoning the matched-history design.

acceptance_items.item: I2/I3 public-mode, schedule, and negative-control coverage

next_gate: Contract complete. Invoke the research workflow to reassess Lab 005 from the earliest unsupported post-stage-1 dependency before any new experiment; performance sampling remains blocked.
